correctness.rationale: For exact endpoint data, the normalized Hermite formula follows by basis interpolation. Its derivative in z is strictly negative for 0<s<=1; consequently the global minimum decreases continuously from 1 to minus infinity and crosses zero at a unique positive z. Endpoint positivity forces the first contact to be a unique interior double zero, and any greater z gives exactly two simple false zeros. A triple zero would change sign and is excluded. Nonzero partial z derivative and positive second s derivative prove square-root unfolding. Exact-rational Taylor-exponential bounds and four-cell Bernstein certificates prove H_(19/5)>0 globally, and H_(39/10)(2/3)<0; thus the numeric root is bracketed independently of numerical root-finding. The bundled verifier confirmed 50 assertions and reproduced numerical constants. No finite grid experiment substitutes for the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The new claim is a complete exponential-decay-specific positive/zero/negative phase transition for unmodified exact-slope Hermite dense output, with an explicit critical constant and local square-root false-event separation. The inspected generic interpolation sources provide formulas, monotonicity and sufficient nonnegativity constraints, but not this sharp exponential threshold and event-bifurcation law. This is a qualified best-knowledge comparison rather than proof of priority; general cubic positivity and bifurcation principles remain known prerequisites.
residual_risks: An exact exponential-decay special case may have been noted in an unindexed plotting, interpolation or event-detection paper.

value.rationale: Exact positive solution values and derivatives provide an unusually strong baseline for evaluating dense-output safety, so fake zero crossings are demonstrably interpolation artifacts, not propagation error. An exact dimensionless step boundary supplies a nontrivial sharp positivity rule, while the explicit square-root separation predicts where spurious event detections appear just beyond the boundary. The independently certified positive/nonmonotone interval at z=7/2 distinguishes positivity from the classical stronger monotonicity requirement. Scope is a natural scalar ODE benchmark and makes no claims about all integrators or event detectors.
